transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today, and what would you like help with?

I’ve been having these really strong beliefs that people are watching me and trying to harm me somehow, and it’s been going on for quite a while now. It feels very real and it’s making me constantly on edge, even though I’m still managing my usual responsibilities. I’d like help understanding what’s happening and how to make this fear calm down.

Over the past few weeks or months, have you felt intensely depressed most of the day nearly every day—such as feeling hopeless, losing interest in things, or thinking life isn’t worth living—or are your mood and energy generally okay apart from the fear and suspicion?

My mood and energy are generally okay apart from the fear and feeling watched. I still do my usual activities and don’t feel hopeless all the time or lose interest in everything, and I haven’t really had thoughts that life isn’t worth living.

Can you tell me roughly how long you’ve been having these beliefs that people are watching or trying to harm you—did they come on very suddenly over days to a couple of weeks, or did they develop gradually and have been present for many months or longer?
They developed gradually, not all at once. I first started noticing these thoughts almost two years ago, and they’ve slowly gotten more persistent over that time.

Apart from feeling watched or targeted, have you noticed other changes like hearing voices when no one is there, feeling your thoughts are being controlled or taken, or having trouble thinking clearly and keeping up with work or self-care, or are those areas mostly unchanged for you?

Those areas are mostly unchanged for me. I don’t hear voices or feel like my thoughts are being controlled or taken, and I’ve been able to think clearly and keep up with work and taking care of myself; it’s mainly the beliefs about being watched and targeted that are the problem.

When you step back and think about it, do you feel completely certain that people are watching and trying to harm you, or is there any part of you that wonders whether this might be your mind playing tricks on you or anxiety making you misinterpret things?

Most of the time I feel completely certain they’re watching me and trying to harm me; it feels very real, not like just anxiety. Once in a while I’ll briefly wonder if I might be overreacting, but that doubt doesn’t last long and I go back to feeling sure it’s really happening.

latest_inference.note: Previously the only candidate was a persistent delusional disorder characterized by non-bizarre persecutory beliefs without prominent hallucinations or marked thought disorder. In this segment, the patient describes a nearly two-year history of gradually developing, fixed persecutory beliefs (being watched and harmed), with preserved mood, energy, work, and self-care, and no hallucinations or first-rank psychotic symptoms. There is only fleeting, minimal doubt about the beliefs, supporting their delusional intensity. There is no evidence of a sustained depressive or manic syndrome, no acute onset, and no significant negative symptoms or disorganization that would push toward other psychotic or mood disorders. Thus, alternative diagnoses have not gained support, and the current candidate list remains the same with F22.0 as the sole working diagnosis. More information about substance use, medical history, and functional impact is still needed, so the interview should continue.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has had a persistent, systematized persecutory delusion (being watched and harmed) for nearly two years, with high conviction and minimal insight, in the absence of hallucinations, formal thought disorder, marked mood syndrome, or significant deterioration in functioning. The gradual onset, long duration, and relative preservation of functioning are most consistent with persistent delusional disorder (F22.0). Acute and transient psychotic disorder with predominantly delusional symptoms (F23.3) is less likely given the chronic course beyond 3 months.
